guide.title: Start with your first block
guide.intro: Create, compile, and upload a project. This guide works offline. Always match the exact board and configuration to your hardware.
guide.createTitle: Create a project and choose a board
guide.createBody: Select New project, choose the actual board, and save. ESP32, S3, and C3 are different targets. For Nano, check the processor and bootloader options.
guide.coreBody: Open Core manager from the new-project board screen. CK recommends 3.3.6-cn for ESP32; AVR uses Arduino AVR Boards. Compilation can detect the environment immediately after installation.
guide.blocksTitle: Build logic and inspect generated code
guide.blocksBody: Add setup and loop blocks, then input, output, or control logic. Manage extensions in Blocks & libraries. Compatibility of third-party blocks depends on the library declaration.
guide.buildBody: Select Compile and inspect live output. The first build prepares dependencies. Later reuse depends on source, board configuration, toolchain, and cache validation.
guide.uploadBody: Connect a data-capable USB cable, select the matching port, and upload. Set the serial monitor baud rate to the value used by the program.
guide.helpBody: Check the board, Core version, complete configuration, and port. Keep the first error and export diagnostics from the build panel. Review files before sharing. A successful compile is separate from physical hardware verification.

drivers.title: Connect your board to CK
drivers.intro: USB drivers depend on the USB chip on your board, not just a board name such as Uno or ESP32. Check the connection before selecting a driver.
drivers.beforeBody: Try a known data-capable USB cable, connect directly to the computer, and watch Device Manager while connecting the board. If a working port already appears, a driver reinstall is usually unnecessary.
drivers.note: CP210x and FTDI download directly from their vendors; other links are mirrors of original packages. Nothing installs automatically. Native USB boards may need no extra driver. Windows may request permission to install a driver.
drivers.downloadBody: Choose by the USB chip or Device Manager entry. You do not need every driver.
drivers.extractBody: A ZIP is an archive. Extract it to a folder before running the installer.
drivers.installBody: Follow the method for your chip below, reconnect the board, then refresh and select its COM port in CK.

methods.pl2303: Extract and run the PL23XX-M_LogoDriver_Setup installer. Check support for older chips first.
methods.cp210x: Extract, then right-click silabser.inf and choose Install (Show more options on Windows 11). Alternatively, update the driver from this folder in Device Manager.
methods.ftdi: In Device Manager, update the driver from the extracted folder with subfolders included. USB Serial Converter and USB Serial Port may each need this step.
